reason: Transfer/leakage lens. (1) The target tail sits almost entirely in one embryo: of the 1,907 a_never FN, 1,740 are 6bba and 167 are 44b6 (91% 6bba), and the top-10 videos, all 6bba, hold 41%. The offset persists per track (the dz sign agrees with the GT predecessor's offset in 82%), and the z-bias depends on the embryo (6bba -0.85 um, 44b6 -0.17 um; per-video q10/q90 -1.34/+0.16). A head trained to reach 7-10 um learns the 6bba annotators' convention. That is the zhincez failure mode (a constant shift lost -0.0031 on the LB), and the private set is ~71% unseen embryos. (2) The OOF protocol is not OOF where it matters. GroupKFold over the head's videos does not make the UNet features out-of-sample: the detector was trained with single-voxel targets at these same GT points on all 199 videos. So a 3x3x3 or 5x5x5 stencil (which widens context to about 3-6 um) can pick up memorised traces of the annotation in the features, and those traces do not exist on test. B26 is the precedent: 43-97% of local TTA gains on pilkwang-initialised models were memorised. Step A/B numbers for any tail recovery would be inflated in a way the proposed folds cannot detect. The raw-image learnability test, which has no memorisation, gives |r| <= 0.09 on the tail and a net rescue of 43/798 (about 5%, the size of a mean shift). (3) The node-count multiplier contaminates the calibration. On the test movies, exp51 (the public head verbatim) cut final nodes 122,704 -> 119,174 (-2.9%, and -10.7% on one video). Through the adjusted-Jaccard factor that alone is worth about 0.1 x 0.029 x 0.95 ~ +0.003, so up to ~40% of x138's +0.007 may be multiplier rather than localisation. The hypothesis's '10% shrink = +0.007' consistency check therefore double-counts. Step B also shifts final nodes without re-running NMS, dedup or the short-track filter, so it freezes node count and cannot see a multiplier change in either direction on the LB. A wider 3 um z cap is the part most likely to move node count, because refined peaks merge or split differently. (4) The measured head moves peaks by a mean of 0.74 um, max 1.61 um: it is a de-quantiser (grid RMS 0.81 um). That part does transfer, since x138 was trained on 20 in-sample train movies and still gained on the LB. The tail-recovery part, which is all of the claimed +0.002..+0.006 above the port, does not survive.
fix_if_any: Drop the gate-aware loss, the track-identity pairs out to 10 um and the 3 um z cap. Keep only a plain de-quantiser retrain: the V1284 architecture, Huber loss on pairs under 4 um, the 2 um bounded output, float output coordinates in both arms. Make it transfer-safe: (a) mandatory embryo folds (train on 6bba, evaluate on 44b6 and the reverse), shipping only if the <4 um share improves over the public head on the held-out embryo by >= +0.005 AND the per-embryo mean shift of the new head stays within +-0.2 um of the public head's (so no embryo-bias learning); (b) subtract the per-embryo mean offset from the training targets, so the head cannot learn an annotation convention; (c) in Step B, re-run NMS, dedup, short-track and linefit on the shifted nodes, or at least report the node-count change and the adjusted-Jaccard factor separately from the edge-J change; (d) since the UNet features are in-sample on all 199 videos, prefer features captured from friend A's leak-free 6bba-only scratch detector for the 44b6 fold as a sanity check, or cap the stencil at the 7-point face stencil (about +-1.6 um) to limit memorisation leakage. Spend the ~2,700 swap and tail FN budget on duplicate or track-level position handling instead.
realistic_public_gain: Gate-aware tail recovery: about 0 (+0.000..+0.0005), with downside risk (an embryo-specific bias like zhincez -0.003) if the wider cap learns the 6bba convention. The plain 199-video de-quantiser retrain over the port: +0.000..+0.002 (a guess; the quantisation ceiling is shared with the public head, which already takes most of it), below the +-0.003 LB noise, so one probe can't confirm it.
